newsitem.title: CHINA: China to allow jv trade firms in Shenzhen, Pudong.
newsitem.headline: China to allow jv trade firms in Shenzhen, Pudong.

text.p: China has allowed the formation of joint venture foreign trade companies in two special economic zones, Shenzhen and the Pudong New Area of Shanghai, the Business News reported on Tuesday.
It said the State Council (cabinet) passed temporary regulations on September 2 to allow creation of such firms, subject to certain conditions. The regulations went into effect on Monday.
The new companies must have a registered capital of at least 100 million yuan, with the Chinese partner holding at least 51 percent and the foreign partner holding at least 25 percent.

The foreign partner must have had a business turnover of at least $5 billion in the year before making its application and annual trade with China of at least $30 million a year in the three years before making its application, it said.
In addition, the foreign partner must have had a representative office in China for at least three years prior to its application or have invested at least $30 million in China, the newspaper said.
As for the Chinese partner, it must have done annual foreign trade business of at least $200 million, including at least $100 million in exports, in the three years before the application, it said.

The Chinese partner must also have at least three subsidiaries, branches or joint-venture companies abroad, with an annual turnover of these businesses in the previous three years of at least $10 million, it said.

The foreign partner must provide its registered capital in a convertible currency, while the Chinese side can provide it in the form of Chinese yuan, physical goods, invisible assets or rights to assets, the newspaper said. It gave no more details. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
